# Fullmoon Economy — full developer reference (LLM-friendly, one page)

Last updated: 2026-09-08. Canonical sources: openapi.yaml (API contract),
fullmoon-sdk README (client), docs/policies.md (rules). If this file and those
disagree, those win.

## 1. What the platform is

The Fullmoon (풀문) network — a Minecraft server network + Discord community —
runs ONE shared currency ("원") on ONE PostgreSQL ledger. Exactly two writers
exist: the coin-bridge Discord bot and the Minecraft plugin. Everyone else,
including all external developers, READS through economy-api:

    coin-bridge bot ──direct SQL──┐
    MC plugin      ──direct SQL──┤→ PostgreSQL (single source of truth)
    external bots ──HTTP GET──→ economy-api ──read-only──┘

There is NO write API and there MUST BE NO second currency. Writing balances,
minting, granting, transferring: impossible over HTTP (removed 2026-07-12;
every non-GET returns 405 before auth). Features that need to grant coins are
built inside the operator's bot, not by opening the API.

## 2. The 3 iron rules (registration-keeping conditions)

1. Never cache balances. The value changes outside your process. Read right
   before display via getAccount().
2. Never create your own currency/balance table. Store non-money state only
   (minigame state, cooldowns, bot settings).
3. Never hardcode balance numbers. Read knobs (multipliers, caps) from
   GET /v1/config and cache ~30s.

Manners: poll at 5s or slower; back off on 429; no traffic floods.

## 3. Quickstart (5 minutes)

1. Ask the Fullmoon Discord operators for a bearer key (name your bot). Keys
   are 32+ random chars, unscoped — read access is the only power.
2. Copy economyClient.js from https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-sdk
   into your project (zero dependencies, Node 18+, ESM).
3. Set ECONOMY_API_KEY. Default base URL: https://api.fullmoon.ink/economy
4. First read:

```js
import { EconomyClient } from './economyClient.js';
const eco = new EconomyClient({ key: process.env.ECONOMY_API_KEY });

const acc = await eco.getAccount(userId);        // { balance, linked, mcUsername } | null
const top = await eco.getLeaderboard(10);        // [{ rank, discordId, balance }]
const wal = await eco.getWalletByMc('SteveMan'); // launcher-shaped, by MC username
```

Smoke check (no auth needed):
curl -s https://api.fullmoon.ink/economy/v1/health
→ { "ok": true, "service": "economy-api", "readOnly": true }

## 4. Endpoints (all GET; base https://api.fullmoon.ink/economy)

Auth: Authorization: Bearer <key> on everything except /v1/health.

GET /v1/health                                   (no auth)
  → 200 { ok, service, readOnly: true }

GET /v1/accounts/{discordId}                     (discordId: 5-25 digits)
  → 200 { ok, discordId, balance, linked, mcUsername, rank }
  rank = ledger ranking by balance (1 = richest), null while the balance is 0.
  → 404 { ok: false, error } — no account YET; accounts appear on first activity

GET /v1/accounts/{discordId}/transactions?limit=10&before=<id>   (limit ≤ 50)
  → 200 { ok, transactions: [{ id, delta, balanceAfter, reason, source, refId,
                               createdAt }], nextBefore }
  newest first. Pass nextBefore as ?before to page backwards (CSV export,
  audit tools). nextBefore is null on the last page.

GET /v1/accounts/by-mc/{username}                (username: [A-Za-z0-9_]{3,16})
  → 200 { ok, wallet: { currency: "원", balance, updatedAt },
          transactions: [{ delta, reason, label, balanceAfter, at }] }
  Launcher/client shaped: resolves the most recently linked account for the
  MC username. `label` is the Korean display label from the ledger vocabulary.
  → 404 when nothing is linked.

GET /v1/leaderboard?limit=10                     (limit ≤ 50)
  → 200 { ok, leaderboard: [{ rank, discordId, mcUsername, balance }] }
  positive balances only, rank starts at 1.

GET /v1/config
  → 200 { ok, config: [{ key, value, description, updatedBy, updatedAt }] }
  Known keys: reward.multiplier, faucet.daily_cap,
  daily.amount, daily.streak_bonus, daily.streak_max_days.
  Read these instead of hardcoding. Cache ~30s.

GET /v1/overview
  → 200 { ok, totalSupply, accounts,
          today: { mint, burn, casinoNet, auctionNet, dropNet, shopNet,
                   transferTax, net },
          bySource: [{ source, faucet, sink, net }] }
  Same classification SQL (TX_FILTERS) as the bot's /경제현황 — numbers cannot
  disagree with in-Discord output.

GET /v1/stats/daily?days=14                      (days ≤ 90)
  → 200 { ok, days: [{ date, mint, burn, casinoNet, auctionNet, dropNet,
                       shopNet, net, activeAccounts }] }

GET /v1/transactions/recent?limit=20             (limit ≤ 100)
  → 200 { ok, transactions: [{ discordId, mcUsername, delta, balanceAfter,
                               reason, source, createdAt }] }
  Global live feed. Poll ≥ 5s.

GET /v1/casino/today
  → 200 { ok, games: [{ game, wagered, paidOut, netBurn }] }

GET /v1/events
  → 200 { ok, events: [{ name, kind, multiplier, startsAt, endsAt }] }
  Currently active events (endsAt null = runs until deactivated). Written by
  the operator only - timer bots just poll this.

GET /v1/guilds
  → 200 { ok, guilds: [{ name, fund, members }] }
  Guild list by fund balance (fund is metadata, not circulating supply).

GET /v1/casino/history?days=30                    (days ≤ 90)
  → 200 { ok, days: [{ date, wagered, paidOut, netBurn }] }
  Per-day casino burn history. netBurn >= 0 = healthy (value destroyed).

Machine-readable contract: OpenAPI 3.1 at
https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-economy-api/blob/main/openapi.yaml

## 5. Error model (client behavior contract)

- 404  → business result: null / empty array. NOT an error. NOT retryable-as-failure.
- 401  → operator problem: throw loudly (bad/revoked key). Contact operators.
- 429  → operator-level limiting: throw; back off and retry. App: 60 req/10s
         per key. nginx: 10 req/s per IP, burst 40.
- 405  → you attempted a write. There is no write API. Stop.
- 5xx  → throw loudly.

The official client (economyClient.js) implements exactly this: it throws on
401/403/429/5xx, returns null/[] on 404, and caches /v1/config for 30s.
Single exception: getConfigValue() swallows read failures and returns the
fallback (config is auxiliary) — use getConfigMap() when you need errors loud.

## 6. Rate limits

| layer | limit |
|-------|-------|
| app (per client key) | 60 req / 10 s (env-tunable) |
| nginx (per IP)       | 10 req/s, burst 40 |

Normal bot traffic never hits these. If you do, you are loop-polling — back
off, and ask the operator for a raise if you genuinely need more.

## 7. Registering a community module

The catalog lives at https://modules.fullmoon.ink and renders the registry JSON
from the SDK repo live — a merged PR appears on the site with no redeploy.

1. Check the 3 iron rules (section 2) — they are keeping conditions.
2. Add an entry to
   https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-sdk/blob/main/registry/modules.json
   following
   https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-sdk/blob/main/registry/modules.schema.json

   Entry shape:
   {
     "name": "My Bot",                        // 1..40 chars
     "type": "bot",                           // bot|dashboard|tool|client
     "description": "한 줄 소개 — 무엇을 보여주는지",  // 5..120 chars, haeyo-che
     "url": "https://invite-or-site-or-repo", // https only
     "source": "https://github.com/you/your-module",  // optional, strongly recommended for bots/tools
     "author": "handle",                      // 1..40 chars
     "addedAt": "2026-09-08",                 // real calendar date
     "verified": false                        // ALWAYS false in a registration PR
   }

Two ways to submit — pick whichever is easier:

- **No git needed**: open a registration issue at
  https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-sdk/issues/new?template=module-registration.yml
  with the fields below; the operator adds the entry for you.
- **PR**: fork fullmoon-sdk, add the entry to registry/modules.json
  (CI validates it), open the PR.

   Entry shape:

Rejections: own balance fields outside the ledger, polling under 5s, ignoring
429, spam links, impersonation.

## 8. Key lifecycle

- Issue: tell the operators your bot's name; they generate a 32+ char random
  key (node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(24).toString('base64url'))")
  and register it in ECONOMY_API_CLIENTS.
- Rotate: report suspected leaks immediately; the operator swaps the key
  (brief downtime possible).
- Revoke: when you retire the integration, the key is removed.

## 9. Security

Found a vulnerability? Do NOT open a public issue. Contact the Fullmoon
Discord operators directly.

## 10. Repo map

- https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-sdk — official client + examples + registry (MIT)
- https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-economy-api — API server source (MIT); src/vocabulary/ is a synced copy of the operator bot's ledger vocabulary — edit the bot first, sync byte-for-byte
- https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-modules — this site (MIT)
- https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/fullmoon-docs — guides + policies (MIT)
- https://github.com/RedHatOnTop/fullmoon-client — Minecraft client (GPL-3.0)
- Public API: https://api.fullmoon.ink/economy — community site: https://fullmoon.ink

## 11. Bot modules (run code inside the Fullmoon bot)

Beyond the HTTP API, the Fullmoon Discord bot itself runs operator-reviewed community modules. A module is one .mjs file with three exports — meta (author/version), command (slash-command name/description/options), execute(interaction, ctx) — plus optional hooks: onButton(interaction, ctx) for button clicks (customIds via ctx.componentId, namespaced cm:<command>:<action>) and schedules = [{ everyMinutes >= 5, run(tools) }] for periodic jobs (max 2/module, 16 bot-wide).

ctx.economy exposes the same audited read-only ledger queries as this API — wallet (balance + rank), transactions (before-cursor pages), leaderboard, events, guilds, casinoToday, casinoHistory — clamped and parameterized, SELECT-only. tools.send (schedules) is text-channel-only, 2000-char capped, user-mentions-only. There is no write path anywhere in the module surface; a feature that needs a ledger write is a bot/operator feature, not a module.

Trust model: modules run in-process, so the operator's line-by-line review is the security boundary. Broken or out-of-contract modules are skipped at load and can never take the bot down. Guide: https://modules.fullmoon.ink/guide.html — contract: https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/coin-bridge-modules/blob/main/MODULE_API.md — submit: PR or issue at https://github.com/Fullmoon-OSS/coin-bridge-modules.
